what_its_for: Travoprost is an eye drop used to lower pressure inside your eye. It is used to treat glaucoma (a condition that can damage your vision) and a condition called ocular hypertension (high pressure in the eye). Lowering eye pressure helps protect your eyesight.
how_to_take: Travoprost comes as eye drops. Always wash your hands before using this medicine. Tilt your head back, pull your lower eyelid down gently to form a small pocket, and place one drop into that pocket. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes and press lightly on the inner corner of your eye (near your nose) with your finger. This helps keep the medicine in your eye and reduces side effects. Do not blink or squeeze your eye hard. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between each medicine.
dosing: Use one drop in the affected eye (or eyes) once each evening. Use it at the same time every night for best results. Do not use more drops than prescribed, as using too much can make the medicine less effective.
missed_dose: If you forget to use your evening dose, skip the missed dose and use your next dose at your regular time the following evening. Do not use two drops in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store the bottle at room temperature, between 36°F and 77°F (2°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat and light. Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Throw away the bottle 6 weeks after opening, even if there is still medicine left. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid letting the tip of the dropper touch your eye, fingers, or any surface, as this can contaminate the drops and cause an eye infection. Do not drive or operate machinery right after using the drops until your vision is clear. Avoid wearing contact lenses in the eye while it is infected or irritated. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant, as this medicine is not recommended during pregnancy.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: sudden changes in your vision or vision loss, severe eye pain or redness, signs of eye infection such as discharge, swelling, or increased redness, swelling of your eyelids, face, or lips (signs of an allergic reaction), or if you accidentally swallow the medicine. Also let your doctor know if you notice your eyelashes getting longer, thicker, or darker, or if the skin around your eye or your iris (the colored part of your eye) changes color, as these can be permanent changes.
when_it_works: Travoprost starts lowering eye pressure within 2 hours of your first dose. It reaches its best effect at around 12 hours. You may not feel any different because high eye pressure usually has no symptoms, but it is very important to keep using it every day as prescribed to protect your vision.
special_populations: Older adults can use travoprost safely at the regular adult dose. Children: Travoprost (Izba) may be used in children aged 2 years and older under a doctor's supervision. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine is not recommended if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. Kidney or liver disease: No dose adjustment is usually needed, but tell your doctor about any health conditions you have.
